subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: Should staff treat the repeated @kingaiwork lookalike pattern as account-level abuse after finalizing the two listing removals, or limit enforcement to these individual records?
rationale: Only authorized staff can inspect the exact production records and audit trail and choose the proportionate account-level trust-and-safety response; public disappearance alone cannot settle that boundary.

options.title: Finalize records and review account
options.body: Confirm both listings are hidden or removed with audit reasons, verify install recovery, and apply the documented account-level enforcement process for the repeated pattern.

options.title: Listing-only enforcement
options.body: Finalize and audit only these two listing actions while leaving the publisher account active under explicit monitoring.

recommendation.title: Finalize records and review account
recommendation.body: Confirm both listings are hidden or removed with audit reasons, verify install recovery, and apply the documented account-level enforcement process for the repeated pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen authored the active namespace-policy RFC and the merged public claim workflow, making them the strongest available routing owner for the unresolved policy and enforcement choice.
